name: link-tabs
description: Route-driven navigation tabs that render real links and mark the current path with aria-current="page".
designIntent: Tabs switch client-side panels; LinkTabs navigates between routes. Settings, account, and app sub-navigation are URL-driven, so they need link semantics, prefix/exact matching, and a router-agnostic link component rather than a tablist.

props.name: items
props.description: Tabs in display order. Each item has label, href, optional exact, icon, and disabled.

props.name: activeHref
props.description: Current pathname used to mark the active tab.

props.name: linkComponent
props.description: Router link element (Inertia Link, Next Link, react-router Link). Defaults to an anchor.

props.name: linkHrefProp
props.description: Prop used to pass the destination to linkComponent: href for anchors/Next Link, to for react-router.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style of the tab strip.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the navigation landmark.

examples.title: Settings sub-navigation
examples.code:
<LinkTabs
  items={[
    { label: 'Profile', href: '/settings/profile', exact: true },
    { label: 'Billing', href: '/settings/billing' },
  ]}
  activeHref={pathname}
  linkComponent={Link}
/>
examples.description: The active item receives aria-current="page"; prefix matching keeps parent sections active on child routes.

antiPatterns.title: Don't use Tabs for route navigation
antiPatterns.explanation: Tabs is a tablist for switching panels in place. Use LinkTabs when the URL changes; screen readers and browser history expect links.

antiPatterns.title: Don't hardcode the active state
antiPatterns.explanation: Pass activeHref from the router; the component handles exact vs prefix matching.

accessibility.implementation: Renders a nav with an accessible label (default "Section").
Native links are tabbable and activate with Enter.
Disabled items render as spans with aria-disabled and no link.

compositionRules.relationship: Place LinkTabs directly below the page header for section navigation.
